guide.intro: Last week: the track. This week: the places the track was made.
guide.outro: You can find where the orders were. Next: what happens when the market goes hunting for yours.

steps.label: CORE CONCEPT
steps.heading: A zone is where an order was filled
body: Before price makes a sharp move it usually does very little — a few small candles in a tight area. That quiet patch is not indecision. It is a large order being accumulated quietly, before the move that shows everyone it exists.
The area of those small candles is the zone. It is drawn from the last quiet candle before the impulse: the top and bottom of that candle's range, extended forward as a band.

It is a band and not a line because the order was filled across a range of prices, not at one. Drawing it as a single line is the most common way beginners make a good idea unusable — price misses their line by twelve cents and they conclude the method does not work.

steps.label: KEY DISTINCTION
steps.heading: A level and a zone are not the same thing
steps.intro: You have used levels since Yellow Belt. A zone is a different object with a different rule.

columns.title: Level — one price
points: Drawn where price turned before
Matters because of memory and round numbers
Either respected or broken, cleanly
Fine on a daily chart, useless at execution zoom

columns.title: Zone — a band
points: Drawn from the base before an impulse
Matters because orders were actually filled there
Has an edge you enter at and an edge that invalidates
Survives the noise a line cannot

steps.note: The practical difference: a level gives you a price. A zone gives you a price to act at AND a price to be wrong at — which is what you need to size a position at Blue Belt.

steps.label: ON THE CHART
steps.heading: Drawing the zone off the base candle
steps.intro: A zone needs two things on the screen: the quiet candle it is drawn from, and the move that left it. One without the other is a guess.
steps.prompt: Tap the base, the candle it ends on, the zone that comes off it, and the leg that proves the whole thing.

marks.name: The base
marks.title: The base · 10:00 to 10:35
marks.body: Eight five-minute candles in which Amazon went from 260.38 to 261.66 — a dollar and twenty-eight cents in forty minutes. Nothing appears to be happening, and that is the point. Quiet is what a large buyer working an order looks like from the outside.

marks.name: The base candle
marks.title: The base candle · 10:35
marks.body: The LAST candle before the move. It traded 261.53 to 261.94 — forty-one cents, the tightest of the eight. This is the one you draw from, because it is the last price at which that buyer could still be filled quietly.

marks.name: The zone
marks.title: The zone · 261.53 to 261.94
marks.body: The base candle's own high and low, extended forward. A band, not a line, because the fills happened across a range of prices. The top edge is where you would act on a return; the bottom edge is where the idea is wrong.

marks.name: The leg away
marks.title: The leg · 10:40 to 10:50
marks.body: From 261.68 to 264.56 in fifteen minutes — more than twice the entire forty-minute base, in a third of the time. The leg is what proves the base was a base. Without a move away this hard, eight quiet candles are just eight quiet candles.

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: Drawing a zone you can actually trade
steps.intro: Four moves, in this order. Skipping the first is how people end up with forty zones on a chart and no decisions.

moves.title: Find the impulse first
moves.body: Look for the move that broke structure — the leg that went somewhere in a hurry. No impulse, no zone. You are looking backwards from a result, not scanning for shapes.

moves.title: Walk back to the last quiet candle
moves.body: From the start of the impulse, step back until the candles go small. That final small candle before the run is the base.

moves.title: Mark its high and low, extend right
moves.body: Two lines from one candle, drawn forward. Not the whole consolidation, not the wick of the impulse — one candle.

moves.title: Mark it used once price returns
moves.body: A zone is spent when price has traded back into it and left again. The orders that made it have been filled. A used zone is history; only unmitigated zones are live.

steps.closing: Three or four live zones on a chart is a working map. Twenty is a wall, and a wall tells you nothing.

steps.label: DEEPER INSIGHT
steps.heading: Why price comes back at all
body: The obvious question is why price would return to a zone rather than simply carry on. The answer is in the first lesson of this belt: the order was never fully filled.

A buyer who wanted two million shares and got six hundred thousand before price ran away still wants the rest. They will not chase — chasing costs them the price advantage they were working for. They leave the balance resting where they were filling, and wait.

That is what an unmitigated zone is: unfinished business. Price returns, the rest of the order fills, and the move continues. Once it has been filled, the reason for the zone is gone — which is why a zone that has already been traded back into is not a zone any more.
Everything in this week reduces to one sentence: find the unfinished business, and stand where it is.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: Price has already returned into a demand zone, bounced, and moved away. What is that zone now?
options: Stronger — it has been proven to work
Spent — the order that made it has been filled
Inverted — it becomes a supply zone
steps.explanation: The zone existed because an order was unfinished. Once price has traded back in, the balance is filled and the reason is gone. Second visits are much weaker than first ones.

wrongFeedback.text: It worked precisely once, and that is what used it up. A zone is fuel, not a wall.
They expire by being used. That is the whole mechanism — unfinished business, then finished.
That is a role flip, which is about a broken level. A mitigated zone is simply spent, not reversed.

steps.reinforce: Unmitigated means untouched since it was formed. Only those are live.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: Where does the invalidation for a demand-zone entry belong?
options: A fixed percentage below the entry
Below the bottom edge of the zone
At the top edge, to keep the loss small
steps.explanation: The bottom edge is the price at which the idea is wrong — the order clearly was not there. A stop above it is inside the noise the zone exists to absorb.

wrongFeedback.text: A percentage knows nothing about this chart. The stop belongs where the idea fails, and the chart says where that is.
That puts the stop inside the zone, so ordinary movement within the band takes you out. Small stops are not the same as good stops.
Backwards, and this is the most expensive habit in trading. The chart sets the stop; the stop sets the size. Never the other way round.

steps.reinforce: The chart decides where you are wrong. Your account decides how much that costs.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: Key takeaways
points: A zone is the quiet base before an impulse — where a large order was being filled.
Draw it from one candle: its high and low, extended forward. A band, never a line.
Price returns because the order was never finished. That unfinished balance is the whole reason the method works.
A zone that price has already traded back into is spent. Only unmitigated zones are live.
The far edge of the zone is where the idea is wrong — which makes it the stop.
steps.closing: Next week: what happens when the market goes looking for the stops everyone put in the obvious place.

match.title: Drill: Draw 3 Zones on Real Charts

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: Three zones, three decisions
body: Three real charts. Each one asks where the zone is, or whether there is one worth having at all. The second answer is right more often than people expect.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Alphabet has gone nowhere for forty minutes — eight candles between 354.01 and 354.67. If price leaves this base upward, where does the demand zone belong?

options.label: On the last quiet candle before the move — its own high and low
At the lowest low, 354.01, drawn as a line

marks.name: The base
marks.title: Forty minutes, sixty-six cents
marks.body: 354.01 to 354.67, eight candles.

marks.name: Base candle
marks.title: 14:35 — the last quiet candle
marks.body: 354.46 to 354.67. Twenty-one cents.

marks.name: The zone
marks.title: 354.46 to 354.67
marks.body: Drawn off one candle, extended forward.

marks.name: The leg
marks.title: 14:40 to 14:45
marks.body: 354.63 to 356.23 in ten minutes.

reveal.headline: The last quiet candle, and only that one
reveal.body:
Alphabet left at 14:40 and was at 356.23 five minutes later. The candle immediately before it, 14:35, traded 354.46 to 354.67 — twenty-one cents. That is the zone.

Draw it across the whole base instead and you have a sixty-six cent band, three times as wide, that any pullback will "reach" — which tells you nothing and costs three times as much when you are wrong. Draw it as a line at 354.01 and price misses you by twelve cents.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla's 341–342 supply, built on 23 July, has now been reached once — on 13 August, which topped at 341.64 and closed back at 339.96. Is that zone still fresh?

options.label: Fresher — it just held, which proves it works
Used — the first visit is where the resting orders start getting filled

marks.name: The supply
marks.title: 341.00 to 342.11
marks.body: Built on 23 July, untouched for fourteen sessions.

marks.name: First visit
marks.title: 13 August · 341.64
marks.body: Forty-seven cents under the top of the band, then closed back at 339.96.

marks.name: Second visit
marks.title: 14 August · through it, to 351.26
marks.body: Opened at 342.33, above the whole band.

marks.name: And back
marks.title: …and back to 335.33 the same morning
marks.body: The same session gave all of it back.

reveal.headline: Used — and the next morning showed you how used
reveal.body:
Every visit fills more of what was resting there. A zone is not a wall that gets stronger with each hit; it is fuel, and the first visit is where the queue starts getting spent.

On 14 August Tesla opened at 342.33, straight through the top of the band, and ran to 351.26. Then the same session handed it all back to 335.33. The band that had stopped price dead three weeks running did not stop it at all the second time it was asked.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla sold from 341–342 on 23 July and has not traded back to it in fourteen sessions. What is that band, right now?

options.label: A spent zone with no further meaning
A demand zone, because price is rising toward it

marks.name: The band
marks.title: 341.00 to 342.11
marks.body: Where the selling on 23 July was filled.

marks.name: The wait
marks.title: Fourteen sessions with no return
marks.body: The closest was 336.20 on 11 August — $4.80 short.

marks.name: The arrival
marks.title: 13 August · 341.64
marks.body: Stopped 47 cents under the top and closed at 339.96.

reveal.headline: Unmitigated supply — and it held on the retest
reveal.body:
Untouched since it formed means the selling that made it was never finished. That is the only thing that makes a zone live.

When Tesla finally got there on 13 August it reached 341.64 — 47 cents under the top of the band at 342.11 — and closed the session back down at 339.96. Real numbers. The band did exactly what an unmitigated zone is supposed to do, and it only got to do it once.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: What the drill was testing
points: One candle makes the zone, not the whole consolidation and not the impulse.
Visits use a zone up. Twice-tested is not twice as strong, it is twice as spent.
Untouched since it formed is the only thing that makes a zone live.

match.title: Live Class: Liquidity Sweeps (The Bait & the Grab)

json.title: Liquidity sweeps — the bait and the grab

guide.intro: The move that makes people quit trading, explained.
guide.outro: You now know why you got stopped out and then watched it go.

steps.label: CORE CONCEPT
steps.heading: Your stop is somebody else's fill

figure.value: A stop loss is a market order with a trigger price.
figure.caption: Which is exactly what a large buyer is looking for

body: When you place a stop below a swing low, you have left a resting sell order at that price. So has everyone else who read the same chart the same way. A shelf of equal lows is therefore a shelf of stop orders, sitting in a known place.

A large buyer needs sellers. Below that shelf is a pile of guaranteed sellers, and the only thing standing between them is a few cents of price. Pushing price down into that shelf is not manipulation in any mysterious sense — it is going where the supply is.
The stops trigger, they sell, the large buyer takes the other side, and then price leaves in the opposite direction. That is the sweep: a move below an obvious low that reverses almost immediately.
It feels personal. It is not. It is arithmetic about where orders are resting.

steps.label: ON THE CHART
steps.heading: The shape a sweep leaves behind
steps.intro: Three things, in this order, and all three have to be on the chart before you can call it a sweep. You saw this morning in Week 1's drill; this is the other name for what it did.
steps.prompt: Tap the shelf, the candles that built it, the candle that took it, and the close that gave it away.

marks.name: The shelf
marks.title: The shelf · 321.05
marks.body: Four candles in a row turned between 321.05 and 321.71 — sixty-six cents apart on a stock that moves six dollars in an hour. That flat underside is a shelf, and every trader who is long above it has left a stop order just beneath it. A shelf is not support. It is a pile of resting sell orders with a sign on it.

marks.name: Where it formed
marks.title: Four candles built it · 9:40 to 9:55
marks.body: A shelf is a run of candles, never one. These four each turned at almost the same price, which is what makes the level obvious enough for the whole market to draw it — and being obvious is exactly what makes it worth attacking.

marks.name: The sweep
marks.title: The sweep · the 10:00 candle
marks.body: One candle does the whole job. Look at its shape: almost all range, almost no net move, and it finishes near the top. If you had to describe it in one word it would be rejection.

marks.name: How far under
marks.title: 320.79 — twenty-six cents through
marks.body: A sweep does not need to go far. It only needs to go far enough to trigger the orders, and those orders sit just under the obvious price. Twenty-six cents cleared four candles' worth of stops, and every share they sold was bought by whoever pushed it down there.

marks.name: The reclaim
marks.title: Closed 323.12 — back above the shelf
marks.body: This is the part that makes it a sweep and not a break. The close is $2.07 above the level it just went through. A break closes below and stays there; a sweep closes back above, and the fifteen minutes after this one took Tesla to 325.45.

steps.label: KEY DISTINCTION
steps.heading: A sweep, or an actual break
steps.intro: Same first half. Completely opposite second half. Getting this wrong is expensive in both directions.

columns.title: Sweep — the trap
points: Spikes through the low, closes back above
Long wick, small body
Sellers below were the fuel
The reversal is the trade

columns.title: Break — the real thing
points: Trades through the low and CLOSES below
Body carries the move, wick is small
The level genuinely failed
The continuation is the trade

steps.note: The distinction is the close, exactly as it has been since Yellow Belt. What changes here is what you do with it: a close back above a swept low is not just 'the level held', it is a signal that the other side has been cleared out.

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: Trading the sweep, not the bait
steps.intro: The order of these matters more than usual — the first two happen before anything interesting is on the screen.

moves.title: Find the obvious low, before the event
moves.body: Equal lows, a well-defined swing, the level everyone would draw. The more obvious it is, the more stops are resting under it, and the more attractive it is to sweep.

moves.title: Wait. Do not pre-position
moves.body: There is no way to know in advance whether the level holds, is swept, or genuinely breaks. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. You are waiting for the market to declare.

moves.title: Require the close back inside
moves.body: The candle must close back above the level. Not trade back above — close. Until then, the more likely reading is a genuine break.

moves.title: Enter on the reclaim, invalidate at the spike low
moves.body: Your idea is that the sweep collected the sellers. If price returns below the spike low, it clearly did not, and you are out with a defined loss.

steps.closing: The reason this works is not that you have found a secret. It is that you waited for the one piece of information — the close — that everyone who got stopped out did not wait for.

steps.label: DEEPER INSIGHT
steps.heading: What changes right after a sweep
body: The sweep is only half the signal. What makes it tradeable is what the market does next, and there is a specific thing to look for: a change of character.

In a downtrend, price has been making lower highs. After a sweep of the lows, watch the first push up. If it takes out the most recent lower high — closing above it — the sequence that defined the downtrend has just been broken for the first time.
That is the change of character. The sweep says the sellers were collected; the break of the last lower high says the buyers have taken control. One without the other is a guess.
This is also why the entry is not at the bottom of the spike. You are not trying to catch the low. You are waiting for the market to prove that the low was the low.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: Price spikes 40 cents below a shelf of equal lows and closes 30 cents above it. What is the most likely reading?
options: A genuine breakdown — the lows have gone
A sweep — the stops under the shelf were filled and price rejected
A supply zone has formed at the spike low
steps.explanation: Below and back above within one candle is the signature. The sellers resting under the shelf were collected and the price would not stay down there.

wrongFeedback.text: A breakdown requires a close below. This one closed above the level it broke.
A great deal changed: everyone with a stop under that shelf is now flat, and their sell orders have been absorbed.
Zones form from a quiet base before an impulse, not from a rejection wick.

steps.reinforce: Below and back above in one candle. That is the shape.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: You spot a beautiful shelf of equal lows. What is the correct action right now?
options: Buy just above the lows, ahead of the sweep
Sell short — equal lows usually break
Nothing yet — wait for the market to declare
Place a buy order under the lows to catch the spike
steps.explanation: A shelf of equal lows can be swept, can break for real, or can simply hold. You cannot know which, and every version of guessing early costs money.

wrongFeedback.text: That is buying the bait. If it is a genuine break you are long into it with your stop in the pile that gets collected.
Sometimes they do. Trading on 'usually', with no confirmation, is the definition of the gambler in this program.
That order fills in the middle of the spike with no idea yet whether price is coming back. You would be catching the knife on purpose.

steps.reinforce: The gambler hopes. The trader waits for the close.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: Key takeaways
points: A shelf of equal lows is a shelf of resting stop orders — a known pile of sellers.
A sweep goes below the shelf and CLOSES back above it. A break closes below and stays.
The signature candle is long wick, small body, closing high in its range.
Wait for the close. Pre-positioning either side of an obvious level is guessing with money.
Sweep plus a break of the last lower high is the confirmation. Sweep alone is half a signal.
steps.closing: Next: the gaps price leaves behind when it moves too fast, and why it comes back to fill them.

match.title: Drill: Find 3 Equal-Lows Charts & Predict the Sweep

json.title: Drill — find equal lows, predict the sweep

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: Three setups, one question each
body: Two of these are about telling a sweep from a break. The third is about doing nothing, which is a skill and is graded like one.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Meta's last three candles all found a floor between 546.39 and 546.80. The 10:00 candle trades to 545.26 and closes at 545.49. Sweep or break?

options.label: Sweep — it went below the shelf
Break — it closed below and did not come back

marks.name: The shelf
marks.title: 546.39 to 546.80
marks.body: Three candles turned in that forty-one cent band.

marks.name: The candle
marks.title: The 10:00 candle
marks.body: Traded to 545.26 and closed at 545.49 — below everything.

marks.name: After
marks.title: The next half hour
marks.body: 543.06 by 10:15, and no close back above the shelf.

reveal.headline: Break — the close is below
reveal.body:
Going below the shelf is not what makes a sweep. Coming back is. Closing at 545.49, ninety cents beneath a floor at 546.39, is the floor failing.

Meta went on to 543.06 by 10:15 and did not close back above the shelf for the next half hour. Buying here on "it must be a sweep" is how a small loss becomes a large one.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla's last two lows sit at 323.88 and 323.85. The 10:15 candle trades to 322.80 and closes at 324.92 — almost no body, a long lower wick. What have you got so far?

options.label: A completed setup — buy the 324.92 close
A sweep. It still needs a close above the last lower high at 324.89

marks.name: The lows
marks.title: 323.88 and 323.85
marks.body: Two candles, three cents apart. The obvious floor.

marks.name: The lower high
marks.title: 324.89 at 10:10
marks.body: The most recent lower high — the sequence that is still pointing down.

marks.name: The grab
marks.title: Traded to 322.80
marks.body: A dollar and five cents under the lows.

marks.name: The reclaim
marks.title: Closed at 324.92
marks.body: Back above the lows, with almost no body left behind.

marks.name: What came next
marks.title: 10:20 closed 326.42
marks.body: Through the 324.89 lower high.

reveal.headline: A sweep — and the confirmation came five minutes later
reveal.body:
The spike to 322.80 filled the stops under the lows, and the close at 324.92 put price back above them. That is the grab, and on its own it is half a signal: the sequence of lower highs, 324.97 then 324.89, was still intact at that moment.

The 10:20 candle closed at 326.42, straight through both of them. That is the change of character, and only now is the setup complete. Tesla was at 328.45 five minutes after that.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla opens 14 August at 342.33, above the 341–342 wall it could not clear for three weeks. It runs to 351.26, then the 10:10 candle closes at 347.03 — back inside the opening range. What was that high?

options.label: A breakout that simply failed on low volume
Liquidity above the wall being taken, with the trapped buyers becoming the fuel down

marks.name: The wall
marks.title: 341.00 to 342.11
marks.body: Three weeks of supply. The session opened above all of it.

marks.name: Opening range
marks.title: 342.01 to 347.80
marks.body: The first fifteen minutes, 9:30 to 9:44.

marks.name: The high
marks.title: 351.26 at 10:05
marks.body: Nine dollars above the wall, forty minutes after the open.

marks.name: Back inside
marks.title: 10:10 closes 347.03
marks.body: Seventy-seven cents back inside the opening range.

marks.name: The unwind
marks.title: 10:15 to 11:25
marks.body: One direction, seventy-five minutes.

marks.name: Where it ended
marks.title: 335.33 by 11:25
marks.body: Six dollars below the wall it had opened above.

reveal.headline: The bait, the grab, and the bill
reveal.body:
Opening above a three-week wall put every breakout buyer in at once, with their stops beneath. The run to 351.26 took the resting orders above the wall — that is the grab, and it is the same mechanism as a sweep of lows, upside down.

The 10:10 close back inside the opening range trapped everyone who bought the break. Their exits are the fuel: 335.33 by 11:25, nearly twelve dollars off the 347.03 close, in seventy-five minutes. Real session, 14 August 2026.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: What the drill was testing
points: Below the shelf is not a sweep. Below and back above, on the close, is a sweep.
The confirmation is the change of character — the first break of the opposing sequence.
Trapped traders are fuel. When a break fails, the people who took it have to get out, and their exit is the next move.
